It’s fair to note that many people have positive experiences with social media, and those perspectives are valid. For a lot of folks, it’s been a lifeline for staying connected to distant loved ones, accessing niche communities, or discovering information they might not have found otherwise. I don’t dismiss those benefits at all—they’re real and meaningful for many. 

That said, my view comes from looking at broader, population-level trends. Studies have linked heavy social media use to increased rates of anxiety and depression in teens, and the algorithmic design of most platforms tends to amplify extreme or divisive content, which has deepened political and social polarization in many countries. I also think about the way it’s reshaped attention spans—shorter, more frequent interactions replacing deeper, more focused engagement. 

It’s not that everyone else is wrong; it’s that we might be weighing different things. You’ve talked to researchers, so I’m curious: what positive impacts did they highlight that stood out to you? Hearing those details might help me see the picture more fully.
